name: form
description: Semantic form element with even-spacing layouts: stacked (default), bordered card, or inline row — native submit and validation untouched.
designIntent: Forms need two things the DOM gives you: a real <form> (submit, Enter, validation) and even, tokenized spacing between fields. Form bakes the layout into variants so field rhythm stays consistent without wrapper divs or one-off gap classes.

props.name: variant
props.description: Visual container: plain vertical stack, bordered card, or inline row with aligned ends.

props.name: gap
props.description: Even spacing between children — token ('md' default) or exact pixels (16).

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Native submit handler — Enter in a text input submits like any form.

props.name: noValidate
props.description: Skip native validation when you drive errors through FormField error props.

examples.title: Stacked settings form
examples.code:
<Form onSubmit={save} noValidate className="max-w-md">
  <FormField id="name" label="Display name" error={errors.name} required>
    <Input value={name} onChange={(e) => setName(e.target.value)} />
  </FormField>
  <FormField id="email" label="Email" error={errors.email}>
    <Input type="email" value={email} onChange={(e) => setEmail(e.target.value)} />
  </FormField>
  <Button type="submit">Save settings</Button>
</Form>
examples.description: Fields space evenly on the md token; errors come from FormField.

examples.title: Card and inline variants
examples.code:
<Form variant="card" gap={16}>…</Form>

<Form variant="inline" onSubmit={search}>
  <FormField id="q" label="Search"><Input type="search" /></FormField>
  <Button type="submit">Go</Button>
</Form>

antiPatterns.title: Don't nest forms
antiPatterns.explanation: Nested <form> elements are invalid HTML — browsers drop the inner form's submit association. Compose with FormLayout sections instead.

antiPatterns.title: Don't fight native validation blindly
antiPatterns.explanation: Passing noValidate means YOU own every error message — pair it with FormField error props or keep native validation on.
antiPatterns.example: <Form noValidate>  // only with client-side validation wired

accessibility.implementation: Renders <form> — Enter-to-submit, browser validation, and autocomplete all work
accessibility.userRequirements: Every control needs an accessible name (FormField provides it)

accessibility.implementation: gap defaults to the md token and accepts exact pixels — rhythm stays consistent across forms
accessibility.userRequirements: Keep related fields closer (smaller gap) than unrelated groups (use FormLayout/Fieldset to group)

compositionRules.relationship: Each field is a FormField; Form spaces them evenly
Multi-column or grouped sections inside a form
Submit button with type="submit" — native Enter handling comes free
